OPEN
This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $N\geq 1$ and let $k(N)$ denote the smallest $k$ such that there exist $N\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$ with\[1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}.\]Is it true that\[\lim_{N\to \infty} k(N)-(e-1)N=\infty?\]
#295: [ErGr80]
number theory | 
unit fractions
Erdős and Straus [ErSt71b] have proved the existence of some constant $c>0$ such that\[-c < k(N)-(e-1)N \ll \frac{N}{\log N}.\]

A partial proof 
claimed by tienxion (using OpenAI GPT-6 (Codex)).
 Summary:
 For each fixed \(B>1\), the note proves an explicit lower bound of order \(N/\log N\) for the excess length when all denominators are at most \(N^{B+o(1)}\). It also shows that bounded excess forces exponential denominators. The argument combines harmonic loss with large-prime cancellation, using connected components to handle primes sharing a denominator.
 Notes:
 This submission concerns quantitative lower bounds under denominator restrictions. It does not claim to solve the unrestricted problem or establish priority for the formulations. GPT-6 through Codex contributed substantially to the derivation, writing, informal proof reviews, and literature search. The source argument was reviewed by the submitting user. The methods have classical antecedents; two relevant historical articles remained inaccessible in full during the literature audit.
